vocabulary.meaning: the main idea of an essay, usually in one sentence
logical connection and flow in writing
giving credit to the source of information
a reason or set of reasons to support an idea
an argument against your main point
the first part of an essay that presents the topic
the final part that summarizes the essay
facts or examples to support your argument
words or phrases that connect ideas
using someone else's work as your own without credit

grammar_tips.title: Using Formal Language
grammar_tips.explanation: Academic essays require formal language. Avoid contractions (use 'do not' instead of 'don't') and slang.

grammar_tips.title: Passive Voice
grammar_tips.explanation: The passive voice is often used in academic writing. Example: 'The results were analyzed.'

example_sentences.sentence: A strong thesis statement guides the entire essay.
Coherence makes your writing easier to understand.
All sources must be cited to avoid plagiarism.
The introduction should outline the main points.
A good conclusion summarizes the arguments and presents a final thought.
